# 4 Maccabees Chapter 14 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal)
**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** Greek MS (Codex Sinaiticus) | **Section:** The Mother's Reason Over Maternal Love

---

**1** Still more admirable is the way in which they urged one another to death through their words of mutual encouragement.

**2** For it was reason that had made them firm in their convictions, and the law that had made them noble, and their love for one another that drove them forward.

**3** For seeing how much they suffered and how steadfastly they endured, even the tyrant and his guards were struck with wonder.

**4** Indeed, even the parents who had raised such children did not grieve at their deaths but rejoiced in their courage.

**5** The mothers who had nursed these brothers were not overcome with grief when they died.

**6** For all women who are devoted to virtue are strengthened by reason, as was the mother of these seven.

**7** When she saw them being tortured one by one, her love for her children did not weaken her resolve to see them die for the sake of the law.

**8** Instead, she watched as each one died and counted it as a spectacle worthy of the greatest joy.

**9** For she loved the law more than she loved her own children.

**10** Her children were noble and obedient, and therefore she urged them on to the struggle.

**11** What was the source of such love for the law in this woman? It was her devotion to God.

**12** For reason devoted to God is able to master even maternal affection when the service of God demands it.

**13** Let no one therefore suppose that a woman is weaker in character or in virtue. For a woman educated in the law proves to be in no way weaker than men.

**14** On the contrary, if we are to speak truthfully, she proves to be stronger — for she was not herself undergoing torture, but was watching seven sons being tortured and enduring it all.

**15** For when reason, through devotion to God, has taken charge of the passions, it governs even a mother's affection for her children.

**16** And surely, just as wise Abraham was ready to sacrifice his son Isaac on the altar for God, and the father's hand was not stayed by compassion for the child,

**17** so too this mother, moved by no compulsion but by her own free choice, sacrificed her seven sons for the sake of God.

**18** Through reason she governed her passions, and she overcame the pain of losing seven sons.

**19** She proved by her faithfulness to God that reason is truly sovereign over the passions, even the most powerful of them.

**20** She is therefore greater than all noble athletes, for she wrestled against passion in the most intimate of arenas — the arena of a mother's heart.

**21** How fitting that she should receive the crown of victory, the crown of imperishable life, for having conquered every passion through reason!
